I do a bit with my tomatoes. On this side of the world i use the Fowler system. It's all pretty simple really.

For tomatoes, i just wash then halve or quarter them. Then you just pack them into the jars and smoosh them a bit too release some juice (enough to cover them). Pack the jars tight with no air gaps. Then they are processed for about an hour (basically the jars are almost covered in cold water which is them heated to near boiling. Need to get the contents to 95 deg Celsius) Most important thing is to get a good clean seal.

The taste of home preserved tomatoes is very close to fresh too. They keep quite well too, recently used a jar from Feb 2016. Apart from a little surface oxidation it was fine.

I use the fowler system which has already been outlined by gumbatron. I would add Make sure your jars are sterile before you start. And once your done label everything, especially if you plan to store it for a few years or you think you might gift them to people.
